title: Lanes, Positioning & Lane Changes
whatItIs: Keep left unless overtaking or turning right, follow lane markings, and change lanes with MSM without forcing anyone to react.
keyFacts: Keep left unless signs say otherwise, or you're overtaking, turning right or passing parked vehicles or pedestrians.
Changing lane: mirrors, a sideways glance if needed, signal, then move when clear.
Don't cut across cyclists when changing lane, including those in cycle lanes.

keyFacts.text: One-way street: traffic MUST travel in the direction shown by signs.
You MUST NOT drive or park in a cycle lane marked by a solid white line during its hours.

keyFacts: In congested traffic don't change lanes unnecessarily.

visual.caption: Which lane to use (Highway Code rules 135, 137–139, 143)

rows: Left lane; right lane to overtake or turn right
Middle or right lane to overtake, then return left
Middle only to overtake or turn right; not the right
Left to go left, right to go right, best lane ahead
Use it if you are slow or others want to overtake

a.label: Cycle lane: solid line
points: You MUST NOT drive or park in it in its hours
Signs may show its hours of operation

b.label: Cycle lane: broken line
points: Don't drive or park in it unless unavoidable
Advice; give way to cyclists in any cycle lane

onTheTest.question: On a three-lane single carriageway, what is the middle lane for?
onTheTest.why: Rule 135: only to overtake or turn right; you have no more right to it than oncoming drivers.

onTheTest.question: A candidate stays in the right lane of a dual carriageway after overtaking. DT1 heading?
onTheTest.why: Rule 137: move back left after overtaking. DT1 12 lists this under Positioning.

traps: Straddling marked lanes is a lane discipline fault.
In slow traffic, don't move to a lane on your left to overtake.
Keep well left on right-hand bends for a better view.
DT1 lists 'not using bus or cycle lanes when the times allow its use' as a positioning fault.
